messages:
maria_support: FYI customer (acct: acme-corp) reporting SSE streams dropping around ~90s, client then reconnects and sees partial duplicated tokens. They say sometimes auth fails on reconnect (401) and billing shows 2 charges for what looks like same request. Posting traces below.

maria_support: Trace snippet from customer: 
```
[client] connected 12:00:01
[server] event: chunk id=xyz token_count=42
[client] disconnected 12:01:35 (no error)
[client] reconnect 12:01:36 last-event-id=xyz?
[server] new request accepted -> returns 200 plus tokens from resumed generation -> duplicate partial output
```

ingrid_eng: thanks, can you confirm if they set Last-Event-Id header or rely on client library? different clients handle reconnection differently.
maria_support: they say using our JS SDK v1.4.1 with builtin reconnect, not manually setting lastEventId.

ingrid_eng: ok. SDK historically did a naive reconnect: open new SSE without last-event-id, then issues resumed generation. That could explain duplicate outputs.
sam_runtime: also want to check whether we convert reconnect into a fresh inference on the backend if KV cache is lost. If client reconnect triggers a fresh server-side invocation but client believes it's resuming, you'll get overlap.

jess_cust: customer: "Sometimes after reconnect we see 401 for a few seconds then normal. It feels like auth token refresh race."

ingrid_eng: that points to our token refresh path. If the SDK refreshes and briefly uses an invalid token, the reconnect handshake may fail -> client retries -> double-invoke.

ops_bot: @ingrid_eng I pulled the gateway logs for acme-corp around these timestamps: 2064509876-2064510200 — showing three connections from same client IP and two distinct inference jobs (job ids j-93 and j-94) within 2s.

ingrid_eng: nice, that matches double-invoke theory. Two things to triage: 1) client reconnect semantics (last-event-id) 2) auth token race causing refused reconnects and client retry. Also need to confirm whether billing dedupe logic treats these as separate charges.
maria_support: customer also attached a tcpdump showing the underlying TCP FIN/ACK from a corporate proxy at ~90s. They suspect a proxy idle timeout.
sam_runtime: proxy idle timeouts are common. When TCP connection dies without SSE server noticing, server may not mark the stream closed immediately and client may not send last-event-id on reconnect. Two mitigation paths: server-side keepalive (comment pings) or upgrade client to use HTTP reconnect + Last-Event-Id on resume.
ingrid_eng: for immediate mitigation we can: 1) enable more aggressive comment pings from gateway (every 25s) to keep proxy alive 2) make SDK send Last-Event-Id on reconnect attempts and include id in the initial handshake so server can attempt to dedupe/resume 3) add server-side short dedupe window (if same client+prompt within 5s, mark as possible retry and avoid double billing).
jess_cust: will customer accept an SDK patch? they prefer server-side fix first.
ingrid_eng: we'll do both. I'll open a runtime PR to add: a) server-side comment-ping <=30s for clients behind proxies b) an idempotency token header support for generation requests so client reconns can pass original request id.
sam_runtime: note: idempotency header must be honored by backend orchestration. If job j-94 arrives with idempotency token matching recent j-93, return same output or an error that signals client to resume.

maria_support: action items for support: ask customer to capture client SDK logs with RECONNECT events and to turn on verbose auth logs. Also ask for their proxy vendor + idle timeout.

ingrid_eng: dev TODOs: create small patch: 
```
// server proto change (pseudocode)
if (header.idempotency_token && seen_recent(token)) {
  return cached_response_for(token)
}
```
Implement comment-ping config behind a feature flag and roll to gateway.

sam_runtime: ops TODOs: temporarily increase gateway comment-ping to 25s for the customer tenant and enable short dedupe window in billing pipeline for 48 hours while we validate.
maria_support: i've scheduled a call with customer tomorrow 09:30 PT to walk through logs and propose SDK update.

jess_cust: thanks team. Quick Q: could TCP keepalive alone have solved this?
ingrid_eng: not reliably: TCP keepalive intervals are often much longer than proxy idle timers and many proxies drop idle HTTP/1.1 connections regardless. Comment pings (SSE comments) are the most portable keepalive.

maria_support: tagging this as sev-2 for now. I'll update customer after ops toggles ping and we ship SDK guidance. :thumbsup:
